title: Complex numbers
summary: A complex number stores two real coordinates: z=a+bi. The symbol i is defined by i^2=-1; a is the real part and b the imaginary part. Complex amplitudes let rotations carry more information than a positive/negative sign.

title: Vectors and ket notation
summary: A column vector is an ordered list of numbers. In a quantum state its entries are amplitudes, indexed by the possible measurement labels. The notation |\psi\rangle (“ket psi”) names the whole column; it is not an extra operation.

title: Matrices as operations
summary: A matrix is a rectangular table of numbers. A square matrix acts on a column vector: each output entry is a weighted sum of input entries. For quantum gates, columns describe where each input basis state goes.

title: Tensor products

title: Normalization
summary: Measurement probabilities must add to one. If amplitudes are a_j, normalization means \sum_j|a_j|^2=1, where \sum_j says “add over all labels j.” The norm is \|a\|=\sqrt{\sum_j|a_j|^2}.

title: Probability and sampling
summary: A probability is a number from zero to one assigning a chance to an outcome. Disjoint outcomes add: if labels 00 and 01 have probabilities 1/8 and 3/8, the chance that the left bit is 0 is 4/8=1/2. This sum is called a marginal probability.

title: Conditional probability
summary: Conditioning means retaining only trials satisfying an event. If A and B are events and P(B)>0, then P(A\mid B)=P(A\text{ and }B)/P(B). The vertical bar means “given.”

title: Basis and basis changes
summary: A basis is a set of independent reference vectors in which every vector has unique coordinates. For one qubit the computational basis is |0\rangle=(1,0)^T, |1\rangle=(0,1)^T. Another orthonormal basis is |+\rangle=(1,1)^T/\sqrt2, |-\rangle=(1,-1)^T/\sqrt2; “orthonormal” means unit length and zero [inner product](/definitions/inner-products/) between distinct members.

title: Inner products
summary: The inner product measures how much one vector aligns with another. Conjugate the first vector's entries, multiply corresponding pairs, and add. A bra \langle u| is the [conjugate transpose](/definitions/conjugate-transpose/) of a ket |u\rangle:

title: Outer products and projectors
summary: An outer product multiplies a column by a row, producing a matrix. It is not the scalar inner product. For normalized u=(1,1)^T/\sqrt2,

title: Conjugate transpose
summary: A dagger \dagger means transpose and complex-conjugate. Transpose exchanges rows and columns; conjugation changes i to -i.

title: Unitarity and reversibility
summary: A matrix U is unitary when U^\dagger U=I. This guarantees preserved lengths and inner products, hence preserved total probability. The dagger is the [conjugate transpose](/definitions/conjugate-transpose/).

title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
summary: Sometimes a matrix acts on a vector only by scaling it. If Av=\lambda v with nonzero v, then v is an eigenvector and \lambda its eigenvalue. The collection of eigenvalues is the spectrum. We need this to identify what phase estimation estimates.

title: Singular values
summary: Singular values describe the stretching of a matrix even when its input and output directions differ. A decomposition A=U\Sigma V^\dagger uses unitary matrices U,V and a diagonal matrix \Sigma of nonnegative numbers \sigma_j. In matching directions, A|v_j\rangle=\sigma_j|u_j\rangle.

title: Reversible computation
summary: A reversible function maps distinct inputs to distinct outputs. Ordinary AND loses information: 00, 01, 10 all produce 0. Retain the inputs and write the answer by XOR into a target to make it reversible:

title: Controlled gates
summary: A controlled gate applies an operation only in the branch where a control bit equals 1. It must preserve coherent superpositions, not measure the control first. With left control and right target, CNOT swaps 10 and 11 and leaves 00,01 unchanged:

title: Ancillas and workspace
summary: An ancilla is an auxiliary qubit or register used to implement a computation. Its role must be specified: scratch space, an oracle target, a success flag, or a phase-estimation register. It is not free memory.

title: Uncomputation
summary: Uncomputation reverses a computation to remove its temporary records. Suppose a reversible circuit computes |x,0\rangle\mapsto|x,g(x)\rangle. After using g(x) to change a phase or another output, apply the inverse circuit to restore the workspace to zero.

title: Measurement
summary: A computational-basis measurement returns one basis label, with probability equal to the squared magnitude of that label's amplitude. For (3|0\rangle+4|1\rangle)/5, it returns 0 with 9/25 or 1 with 16/25. It does not print the amplitudes 3/5 and 4/5.

title: Global and relative phase
summary: A phase is a unit-magnitude complex factor, e^{i\theta}. A global phase multiplies every amplitude by the same factor; it changes no measurement predictions. A relative phase changes some amplitudes relative to others and can alter later interference.

title: Density matrices
summary: A density matrix represents both pure states and classical uncertainty about prepared states. For a pure state |\psi\rangle, it is the [outer product](/definitions/outer-products/) \rho=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|. For a mixture that chooses state \psi_j with probability p_j, it is \rho=\sum_j p_j|\psi_j\rangle\langle\psi_j|.

title: Observables and expectations
summary: An observable is represented by a Hermitian matrix O=O^\dagger. Its eigenvalues are the possible numerical outcomes in its eigenbasis measurement. The expected value is \langle\psi|O|\psi\rangle, or \operatorname{Tr}(\rho O) for a mixture.

title: Query, gate, and runtime complexity
summary: A query is one use of a specified oracle. Gate complexity counts elementary logical operations, including the oracle's implementation if it is not treated as a free box. Runtime also includes scheduling, state preparation, repetitions, readout, classical work, and error correction.

title: Classical and coherent oracles
summary: An oracle specifies how the input problem can be accessed. A classical oracle accepts a classical x and returns f(x). A coherent reversible oracle is the unitary U_f|x,y\rangle=|x,y\oplus f(x)\rangle, including its action on superpositions. Coherent access is a different interface, not a classical API called on a Python list.

title: State preparation
summary: An algorithm needs a circuit that creates its input state. Writing a normalized vector is not enough. Uniform amplitudes over 2^n labels are easy: apply H to each of n zero qubits.

title: Reversible arithmetic
summary: Arithmetic inside a quantum algorithm must be a reversible circuit. Addition can retain its input and act modulo a fixed power of two: on a two-bit target, add 1 via the permutation 0\to1\to2\to3\to0. Its inverse subtracts 1.

title: The Hadamard test
summary: This circuit estimates the real part of \langle\psi|U|\psi\rangle using controlled-U. Prepare control 0 and target \psi, apply H to control, then controlled-U, then H again. The joint state becomes

title: The SWAP test
summary: The SWAP test estimates squared overlap of two pure states. Prepare control |0\rangle and target registers |u\rangle|v\rangle. Apply H, controlled exchange of the two targets, then H. The control-0 branch is (|u\rangle|v\rangle+|v\rangle|u\rangle)/2.

title: Expectation-value estimation
summary: Suppose measuring an observable returns values +1 or −1. Averaging m independent prepared-and-measured shots estimates its expectation. If 75 of 100 shots return +1, the estimate is (75-25)/100=0.5.

title: Modular arithmetic
summary: a\bmod N is the remainder after division by positive integer N. For example 17\bmod5=2. Congruence a\equiv b\pmod N means the two remainders agree. You may reduce after each multiplication: 3^4\bmod7=(2^2)\bmod7=4 because 3^2\bmod7=2.

title: Continued fractions and rational reconstruction
summary: Fourier measurement often gives a fraction close to s/r, with unknown period r. A continued fraction writes a real number as an integer plus the reciprocal of another such expression. Truncating it gives especially accurate rational approximations, called convergents.

title: Linear equations modulo two
summary: In binary linear algebra, addition is XOR and multiplication is ordinary multiplication of bits. Everything is reduced modulo 2. An equation s_0\oplus s_2=0 says the two bits agree.

title: Hamiltonians and time evolution
summary: A Hamiltonian H is a Hermitian matrix describing energy and generating time evolution. In units where the constant \hbar=1, evolution for time t is e^{-iHt}. Unlike a measured energy, this is an operation on amplitudes.

title: Polynomials as matrix transformations
summary: A polynomial is a finite sum of powers with coefficients, such as p(x)=3x-4x^3. Its degree is the highest nonzero power, here 3. At x=1/2, p(1/2)=3/2-4/8=1.

title: Groups, characters, and hidden subgroups
summary: A group is a set with an associative combining rule, an identity, and an inverse for each element. Integers modulo 4 with addition form a group: identity 0, inverse of 1 is 3. It is abelian because order of addition does not matter.
